sections.label: CRS and PIC amendments
sections.summary: Amendments let Singapore implement the Common Reporting Standard and give effect to 2016 Budget changes to the PIC scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The first set of amendments allows Singapore to implement the Common Reporting Standard (CRS), an internationally agreed standard for automatic exchange of financial account information.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The second set of amendments gives effect to the changes announced in the 2016 Budget Statement to the Productivity and Innovation Credit (PIC) scheme.

sections.label: PIC payout rate and e-filing
sections.summary: The PIC cash payout rate falls from 60% to 40% for qualifying expenditure from 1 August 2016, and electronic filing becomes mandatory then.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: First, as we move towards more targeted measures under the Industry Transformation Programme as announced during the recent Budget, the PIC cash payout rate will be lowered from 60% to 40% for qualifying expenditure incurred on or after 1 August 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Second, to streamline and expedite processing of PIC cash payout applications, electronic filing of PIC cash payout applications will be made mandatory from 1 August 2016.

sections.label: PIC claims audits and clawback
sections.summary: Indranee Rajah said 102,000 companies benefited from PIC; only 30% of 2011-2015 claims were audited, 2.1% required clawback, and $11 million was clawed back for 2011-2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As stated by Senior Minister of State Indranee Rajah in March, since its inception until January this year, 102,000 companies, or 70%, of all active companies in IRAS' records for the Year of Assessment 2014 have benefited in one way or another from the PIC scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As previously mentioned also by Senior Minister of State Indranee Rajah, IRAS does conduct rigorous compliance programmes to review and audit PIC claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, only 30% of claims from years of assessment 2011 to 2015 have been investigated or audited and about 2.1% of these claims investigated required clawback.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For years of assessment 2011 to 2014, IRAS has clawed back $11 million.

sections.label: Sums from dubious claims
sections.summary: Sums not given out or recovered from dubious claims totalled about $358 million in the last five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The sums not given out or recovered from these dubious claims amounted to about $358 million in the last five years." This means that IRAS is either spending a lot of resources weeding out inaccurate or false claims or spending a lot of resources trying to claw back funds already paid out.

sections.label: Support for CRS amendments
sections.summary: The speaker supports Income Tax (Amendment No 2) Bill amendments for Singapore to implement CRS from 1 January 2017, with AEOI starting 2018.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: International clients should choose to bank in Singapore on the strengths of our broad and deep capabilities in financial products and services, strong regulatory regime and rule of law, and not because they think they can abuse our laws to evade paying tax.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I support the proposed amendments to the Income Tax (Amendment No 2) Bill to allow Singapore to implement the Common Reporting Standard (CRS) with effect from 1 January 2017, a move that improves our international tax compliance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: This is in line with Singapore's commitment to commence automatic exchange of financial account information (AEOI) in 2018.

sections.label: CRS compliance costs for FIs
sections.summary: Implementing CRS and AEOI will add significant compliance costs to financial institutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Second, the implementation of CRS and AEOI will add significant compliance costs to FIs.

sections.label: Prioritising countries for CAAs
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to lay out how Singapore will prioritise countries for CAAs and estimated timelines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: To this end, I would like to ask the Minister to lay out clearly how Singapore will prioritise the countries that we sign CAAs with, together with estimated timelines.

sections.label: Automatic exchange of tax information
sections.summary: The speaker recalls 2013 assurances on IRAS safeguards and asks how clients will regard tax information integrity and privacy under an automated exchange regime.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: In my speech in 2013, I spoke on the amendment that gives IRAS the right to access information protected under the Banking Act and the Trust Companies Act for Exchange of Information, without having to first obtain a Court Order.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I was assured by the then Senior Minister of State  Josephine Teo that robust safeguards have been put in place by IRAS, including the need for foreign jurisdictions to explain why the request is being made, identify the taxpayer under investigation or assessment, and declare that it has pursued all available means in its own jurisdiction to obtain the information.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Yet, in less than three years, we are asked to consider a regime that automates the exchange of sensitive information.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: How will FI clients regard the rigour with which we safeguard the integrity of their tax information and the individual's right to privacy?

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, we need to guard against regulatory arbitrage, implementation complexity and systemic leakage and misuse of information exchange.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: FI clients must ready themselves for a new age of unprecedented transparency and big changes to tax regimes, as governments work hard to get what is due their peoples.

sections.label: Conditions for bilateral AEOI arrangements
sections.summary: Singapore will consider bilateral AEOI arrangements only with appropriate partners, subject to three conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As AEOI entails the transmission of information between jurisdictions, Singapore will consider entering into bilateral AEOI arrangements only with appropriate partners, subject to three conditions.

sections.label: Prioritising AEOI with UK and France
sections.summary: Singapore will prioritise AEOI with jurisdictions meeting the stated conditions, such as the UK and France.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In this regard, Singapore will prioritise AEOI with jurisdictions which meet the conditions stated, such as the UK and France.

sections.label: Claims rejected upfront
sections.summary: Of 71,000 claims, about 44,000, or 62%, were rejected upfront before any cash was disbursed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Of these 71,000 claims, about 44,000 claims, or 62%, were rejected upfront even before any cash was disbursed.

sections.label: Completed claim investigations outcomes
sections.summary: Of 21,500 claims with completed investigations, 20,000 were in order and 1,500 required clawback.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Of the 21,500 claims for which investigations have been completed, 20,000 were in order and 1,500 required clawback.
